title: Keeping PIM Busy: Eliminating Execution Overheads for Full Throughput
evidence_span: A multi-channel PIM emulation platform finds PIM cores active only 6.55% of execution time; Channel-Level Burst, PDMA, and an integrated PIM core address host communication, DMA request generation, and serialized bank execution, with reported component speedups of 9.10x, 29.6x, and 102.4x and combined 145.8x improvement over baseline.
problem: PCIe-based PIM systems underutilize memory bandwidth because host communication, request generation, and bank execution serialize work.
method_or_artifact: Co-designed channel operand generation, PIM-oriented DMA scheduling, and multi-batch PIM core execution.
workload_or_benchmark: GEMM microbenchmarks and four LLMs on a multi-channel PIM emulation platform; models, channels, baseline, and measurement boundaries are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: PCIe-connected multi-channel PIM with per-bank execution and host DMA; memory technology, bandwidth, and emulator fidelity are unspecified.
baselines: conventional DMA and serialized bank execution
limits: The description omits absolute throughput, energy, emulator validation, communication traffic, and component interaction effects.
Multiplicative component gains may not compose under full workloads or hardware constraints.
Official description only; PIM claims require paper-level and hardware verification.

title: Parallel Combinational Equivalence Checking Through Factored Form Sharing
evidence_span: The ABC implementation uses factored-form literal count and branching-complexity estimates to partition equivalence problems for literal/CNF reuse; on large benchmarks with 40 CPU cores it reports 45.57x geometric-mean speedup over single-threaded ABC, 1.53x over a CPU-parallel method, and 5.52x over a GPU-parallel method.
problem: Combinational equivalence checking becomes time-critical as designs scale, and parallel SAT solving suffers from duplicated literals and unbalanced branching complexity.
method_or_artifact: Sharing-aware seed-and-grow partitioning guided by factored-form literal count and branching proxies.
workload_or_benchmark: Large-scale combinational-equivalence benchmarks on 40 physical CPU cores; benchmark suite, timeout policy, hardware, and competing tool versions are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: ABC-based SAT/CNF equivalence checking on multicore CPU and GPU baselines; solver configuration and memory system are unspecified.
limits: The description omits absolute runtimes, solved/timeout counts, memory use, benchmark composition, and fairness of core/GPU comparisons.
Sharing benefits may depend on structural regularity and SAT encoding choices.
Official description only; equivalence and scalability claims require reproducible benchmarks.

title: StepPRM-RTL: Stepwise Process-Reward Guided LLM Fine-Tuning for Enhanced RTL Synthesis
evidence_span: StepPRM-RTL combines stepwise trajectory modeling, process-reward modeling, retrieval-augmented fine-tuning, and Monte Carlo tree search to provide dense intermediate feedback for RTL generation; benchmark Verilog/VHDL evaluation reports improvement over standard supervised or outcome-based training, without numeric values in the official description.
problem: Long-horizon RTL generation requires multi-step reasoning and strict functional correctness that outcome-only LLM training does not reliably provide.
method_or_artifact: Stepwise reasoning trajectories, process-reward model, RAFT fine-tuning, and MCTS path exploration for RTL synthesis.
workload_or_benchmark: Benchmark Verilog and VHDL datasets; correctness tests, design distribution, model base, and comparative metrics are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: LLM-generated RTL compiled and functionally evaluated; HDL tools, synthesis targets, prompt context, and compute budget are unspecified.
metrics: Improved functional correctness and reasoning fidelity claimed qualitatively
limits: The description omits pass rates, synthesis quality, reward calibration, training cost, and failure cases.
Reasoning traces do not guarantee executable or synthesizable RTL correctness.
Official description only; LLM-EDA claims require artifact and independent test verification.

title: Pimony: A DRAM-PIM Design for Harmonizing PIM and Memory Accesses with Minimal Interference
evidence_span: PIMony enables concurrent PIM and conventional DRAM operations with interrupt-based asynchronous, preemptible MAC execution and Dual-Path Subarray Access using dual-row activation; the description claims improved co-execution efficiency and stable LLM decoding latency under concurrent memory accesses.
problem: On edge devices, DRAM-PIM operations contend with host memory requests, creating bank conflicts and global stalls during LLM inference.
method_or_artifact: Asynchronous interruptible PIM execution and dual-path subarray access for concurrent PIM/host operations.
workload_or_benchmark: Edge-side LLM inference with concurrent PIM and memory traffic; DRAM organization, models, latency, throughput, and baselines are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: DRAM-PIM architecture supporting dual-row activation and preemptible MACs; timing, circuit feasibility, bank count, and memory standard are unspecified.
metrics: Stable LLM decoding latency claimed qualitatively
limits: The description omits numerical throughput, latency, energy, area, timing closure, and interference measurements.
Dual-row activation and interruptible PIM may impose circuit/control overheads or reliability constraints.
Official description only; architecture claims require paper-level simulation or silicon evidence.

title: Dart: Towards Redundancy-Free RTL Simulation via DAG-Driven Execution
evidence_span: Dart builds a DAG intermediate representation exposing common subexpressions across stimuli, evaluates shared logic once, and reconstructs per-stimulus state to preserve correctness; the official description positions this against CPU/GPU simulators that execute each stimulus independently, without numeric results.
problem: RTL simulation redundantly recomputes identical internal states across stimuli, limiting scalability as SoC complexity grows.
method_or_artifact: DAG-driven intermediate representation, sub-DAG merging, shared computation execution, and lightweight state reconstruction.
workload_or_benchmark: Multiple-stimulus RTL simulation; circuit suite, stimulus count, correctness checks, and speedup metrics are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Pre-silicon RTL simulation on CPU/GPU or custom execution engine; simulator semantics, memory, and event scheduling details are unspecified.
limits: The description omits runtime, memory overhead, event-semantic coverage, stimulus diversity, and numerical comparison.
DAG merging may be limited by divergent state or timing semantics.
Official description only; simulator correctness and performance require artifact verification.

title: Toward True-3D Timing-Driven Analytical Global Placement for Mixed-Size Face-to-Face 3D ICs
evidence_span: The framework integrates drive-strength cell delay, L-shaped RC net delay, and STA-based incremental timing criticality into true-3D analytical placement, with macro-boundary-aware initialization for mixed-size face-to-face 3D ICs; numerical outcomes are not included in the official description.
problem: Timing optimization remains underdeveloped in analytical placement for mixed-size face-to-face 3D ICs with vertical interconnects and hybrid bonding.
method_or_artifact: Timing-driven net weighting and differentiable macro-boundary-aware true-3D initialization adaptable to 3D and multi-die 2D placement.
workload_or_benchmark: Mixed-size face-to-face 3D IC placement with STA and RC timing; designs, technology, timing metrics, and baselines are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Hybrid-bonded or micro-bump 3D ICs with multi-die placement and vertical interconnect; process, thermal, power, and bonding constraints are unspecified.
limits: The description omits wirelength, timing, congestion, thermal, and runtime results.
RC and STA approximations may not capture bonding, thermal, or signoff effects.
Official description only; physical-design claims require paper-level signoff validation.

title: VeRA+: Vector-Based Lightweight Compensation for Drift-Resilient RRAM In-Memory Computing
evidence_span: VeRA+ reuses shared projection matrices and two drift-specific vectors per drift level, selecting offline-trained parameters without on-chip retraining or replay; it preserves up to 99.77% drift-free accuracy after ten years of simulated drift, reduces storage overhead by over three orders of magnitude versus BN calibration, and uses one-week drift measurements from fabricated 1T1R RRAM.
problem: RRAM conductance drift degrades long-term CIM accuracy, while retraining, rewriting, and batch-normalization calibration impose storage and energy costs.
method_or_artifact: Lightweight vector compensation with drift-aware scheduling and measured-device drift statistics.
workload_or_benchmark: RRAM IMC neural inference under ten-year simulated drift and one-week fabricated 1T1R measurements; model, task, drift distribution, and baseline details are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Fabricated 1T1R RRAM CIM array with conductance drift and offline parameter storage; array scale, ADC/DAC, temperature, and endurance are unspecified.
metrics: Up to 99.77% of drift-free accuracy after ten years simulated drift
Over three orders of magnitude lower storage overhead than BN calibration
limits: The description omits absolute accuracy, energy, latency, temperature, device count, and cross-chip variation.
Ten-year simulation depends on drift extrapolation from one-week measurements.
Official description only; endurance and accuracy claims require device-level verification.

title: PLONK-Hammer: Breaking Input Privacy of PLONK Proving Systems via Rowhammer
evidence_span: PLONK-Hammer injects Rowhammer faults into secret inputs, recovers them from faulty proofs using polynomial-commitment techniques, and is evaluated against the gnark implementation to leak secrets.
problem: The fault-injection resilience of PLONK zero-knowledge proving systems is less established than their cryptographic attack resistance.
method_or_artifact: Rowhammer fault injection combined with faulty-proof analysis and polynomial-commitment recovery.
workload_or_benchmark: gnark PLONK proving system with secret-input fault injection; hardware platform, memory layout, proof parameters, repetitions, and recovery success are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: DRAM Rowhammer-capable system running PLONK/gnark; memory technology, privileges, refresh settings, and fault model are unspecified.
metrics: Secret leakage demonstrated on gnark claimed qualitatively
limits: The description omits attack distance, success rate, mitigations, proof parameters, and required privileges.
A gnark demonstration may not generalize across implementations or DRAM platforms.
Official description only; cryptographic-security claims require responsible-disclosure and reproducibility review.

title: Voyager: An End-to-End Framework for Design-Space Exploration and Generation of DNN Accelerators
evidence_span: Voyager is an HLS-based DNN-accelerator generation and DSE framework with configurable processing elements, buffers, bandwidth, technology nodes, frequencies, datatypes, and quantization schemes, integrating software compilation; the official description claims broader configurability and tapeout-oriented generation than prior tools without numeric results.
problem: Existing DNN accelerator generators have limited parameterization, weak datatype/quantization support, and lack an integrated compiler for end-to-end design exploration.
method_or_artifact: Configurable HLS accelerator generator, multi-parameter design-space exploration, and integrated software compiler.
workload_or_benchmark: DNN accelerator workloads across technology nodes and quantization schemes; model suite, generated-design quality, PPA, compiler coverage, and baselines are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: HLS-to-accelerator flow with configurable PEs, buffers, bandwidth, clocks, technologies, and datatypes; synthesis tools and implementation constraints are unspecified.
metrics: Broader parameterization and datatype support claimed
limits: The description omits PPA numbers, synthesis validity, compiler correctness, search cost, and technology-node evidence.
